text: A mother and her daughter were just killed in a suspected grizzly attack on a trail in Canada.
Jennifer Balcarras and her twenty year old daughter Selah Reed went for a walk near Bella Coola on Saturday.
The trail is only five minutes from their home. They never came back.
Searchers found them on Monday and Tuesday. Officials believe a grizzly was involved and they are still trying to catch it.
So what should you do if a grizzly comes at you?
Don't run. A grizzly is as fast as a racehorse and running can make it chase you.
Most charges are bluffs. Stand still and talk to it in a calm low voice.
Pull out your bear spray and fire it at the bear's face when it gets close.
In one big study bear spray stopped grizzlies more than nine times out of ten.
If it grabs you play dead. Lie flat on your stomach with your pack on and your hands behind your neck.
Spread your legs so it can't flip you over and stay still until it leaves.
If it keeps attacking fight back hard and hit it in the face.
Walk in groups make noise and keep bear spray where you can grab it fast.
Rest in peace Jennifer and Selah.
